title: Pupil/gaze behavioral QC (Task 3) and descriptive covariation with independent neural pre-state quantities (Task 4)
purpose: Task 3 (QC across a representative session subset) and Task 4 (descriptive covariation between pre-event pupil/gaze features and independent neural pre-state quantities) of the pupil/gaze behavioral-covariate vetting effort, gated by omission/artifacts/.lab/pupil-gaze-semantics-audit-20260828.json. This is descriptive evidence -- it does NOT prove or disprove a gain/state confound and does NOT run the synthetic gain-confound calibration estimator (out of scope per the task's own instruction).

receipts.raw_result: C:/Users/nejath/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/.../scratchpad/behavioral_qc_covariation_result.json (full per-session QC table, grouped KW tests, and all 36 per-session correlation records -- this receipt summarizes it, does not replace it as the source of the exact numbers)

sampling.rationale: 6/22 sessions (27%), 2 per subject -- covers all 3 subjects and both h5py layout variants (C31o/V198o flat, V182o nested), and deliberately includes sub-V198o_ses-230629_rec (the shortest/most atypical session per the prior trial-count inventory) to check length-sensitivity. Same 6 sessions were already read at the pupil/gaze VALUE level for the Task 1 semantics audit, so this receipt shares an evidence base with that audit rather than introducing a fresh unverified sample.
sampling.window: shared pre-event p1-anchored window, (-500, 0) ms, for pupil and gaze; LFP/MUAe baseline used (-500, 1) ms (load_analog_epochs requires a sample AT t=0 -- the extra 1 ms includes the p1-onset sample itself, negligible in a 501-sample mean-power calc, a stated Task-4-only simplification not used for any behavioral feature).
sampling.neural_area_used_per_session: V1 preferred where available (C31o both sessions, V198o both sessions); V182o's probes in this corpus subset carry no V1 -- fell back to PFC (the most common area on V182o's probes) for both V182o sessions. This is a stated compute-budget simplification (one area, not all channels/probes), not a claim that V1/PFC is the scientifically preferred area for this comparison.
sampling.firing_rate_covariate: population mean pre-event firing rate across up to 10 stable_plus units (row-order subset, a stated pragmatic compute-budget cap, not a scientific unit selection), same window/anchor as LFP/MUAe.

task3_qc_summary.headline: Under this module's stated QC heuristic (no ground-truth invalid-sample marker exists in this corpus -- see the Task 1 semantics audit), essentially ALL trials pass QC (pupil_qc_pass_frac and gaze_qc_pass_frac == 1.0 in every one of the 6 sessions; mean valid_frac >= 0.9999 in every session). This is expected given the semantics audit's own finding that the clip-proximity/NaN heuristic rarely fires (near-zero pct_at_min corpus-wide) -- it means the heuristic is NOT catching meaningful invalidity, not that the data is flawlessly clean. Discontinuity counts (a SEPARATE heuristic, sample-to-sample jumps > 5 SD within a trial's own window) are far more informative and show REAL, LARGE, session-dependent variation: 0% of trials show any discontinuity in both V182o sessions, 8-10% in both C31o sessions, but 47% (sub-V198o_ses-230719_rec) and 84% (sub-V198o_ses-230629_rec, the short/atypical session) of trials in V198o. This is a genuine, receipted finding: V198o's pupil channel is noticeably noisier/more discontinuous by this heuristic than the other two subjects', and the shortest session is the worst of all -- consistent with, but not proof of, a real data-quality difference (possibly an artifact of that session's own short/atypical recording, per the prior inventory's own flag on this session).
task3_qc_summary.per_session_table: see raw_result.per_session_qc for the full table (n_trials, qc_pass_frac, mean_valid_frac, outlier_frac_robust5mad [5x-MAD robust-z outlier rate on qc-passing trials], clip_proximity_frac, discontinuity rate, pupil/gaze summary stats). Reproduced here as a compact summary:
task3_qc_summary.outlier_criterion_stated: A qc-passing trial's mean feature value is flagged an outlier if |value - session_median| > 5 * (1.4826 * session_MAD) -- a robust (median/MAD-based, not mean/SD-based) z-score threshold of 5, chosen to be conservative (few false positives) given the already-noted absence of a ground-truth validity marker.
task3_qc_summary.gaze_excursion_criterion_stated: No calibrated screen-boundary exists (units are not physical, see Task 1 audit) -- 'excursion' here is the SAME robust-z outlier criterion applied to dist_from_center, not a true off-screen detector.
task3_qc_summary.not_done_as_literally_specified: The task's 'impossible pupil values (e.g. non-positive diameter)' criterion does NOT apply to this corpus -- the Task 1 semantics audit established the stored pupil quantity is NOT raw diameter (56-72% of samples are already non-positive as a structural feature of the transform, not an error). Applying a non-positive-is-impossible rule here would flag the majority of all data as invalid, which is not a defensible QC criterion for a transformed signal -- reported as a deviation from the task's literal wording, not silently substituted.

grouped_statistical_tests.methodology: Per omission-statistics doctrine (session-aware, not naive pooled): (1) within-session condition/omission-slot effects tested via one Kruskal-Wallis PER SESSION across its own conditions (trial-level, valid within one session's own baseline); (2) a trial-level cross-session KW is also reported but explicitly labeled DESCRIPTIVE-ONLY because sessions are not independent replicates of one condition; (3) the primary cross-subject/cross-session claim uses session as the unit of replication (one value per session, its median feature value) to avoid pseudo-replication across trials within a session.
grouped_statistical_tests.within_session_condition_effect: pupil_mean: significant at p<0.05 in 2/6 sessions (sub-C31o_ses-230816_rec p=0.042, sub-V198o_ses-230629_rec p=0.041 -- the latter on only 38 trials across 5 conditions, low power); NOT significant in the other 4/6. gaze_dist_from_center: significant in 1/6 sessions (sub-V198o_ses-230629_rec p=0.028). No multiplicity correction applied across the 6 sessions x 2 features = 12 tests -- at alpha=0.05 uncorrected, ~0.6 false positives are expected by chance alone among 12 tests, so these few significant results should NOT be read as a confirmed condition effect without independent replication or correction.
grouped_statistical_tests.cross_session_trial_level_kw_descriptive: Both features show p~0 at the trial level pooled across all 6 sessions (pupil H=1680, p<1e-300; gaze H=143, p=4e-29) -- as labeled, this is NOT a valid inferential claim (huge N from pseudo-replicated trials within sessions with different baselines trivially produces significance); included only because the task asked for it, immediately superseded by the session-as-unit test below.
grouped_statistical_tests.cross_subject_session_as_unit_kw: Using session-level median as the unit of replication (n=3 subjects, 2 sessions each): NOT significant for either feature (pupil H=4.57, p=0.10; gaze H=3.43, p=0.18). With only 3 subjects this test has very low power and a null result here should not be over-interpreted as 'no subject effect' -- it is consistent with, but far from conclusive evidence against, one.
grouped_statistical_tests.full_numbers: see raw_result.grouped_stat_tests for exact per-session H/p values.

task4_covariation_summary.headline: Real, but SESSION-DEPENDENT and SIGN-INCONSISTENT descriptive covariation exists between pre-event pupil/gaze features and independent neural pre-event quantities (LFP baseline power, MUAe baseline power, population pre-event firing rate), computed per-session via Spearman correlation on qc-passing, trial-id-matched trials (session-aware -- no pooling across sessions). This is DESCRIPTIVE ONLY, explicitly NOT a confounding proof and NOT a claim about mechanism or directionality (per this project's own doctrine on association vs. causality).
task4_covariation_summary.methodology_note: 36 correlation tests total (6 sessions x 2 behavior features x 3 neural features), no multiplicity correction applied -- reported as raw per-session Spearman rho/p, with the count of tests stated here so a reader can judge the risk of chance findings among the smaller p-values.
notable_findings: pupil_mean vs lfp_baseline_power: significant positive in 3/6 sessions (sub-C31o_ses-230823_rec rho=0.394 p=1.3e-7 n=168; sub-V182o_ses-260710 rho=0.426 p=8.6e-9 n=168; sub-V198o_ses-230629_rec rho=0.323 p=0.048 n=38 -- borderline, small n), NOT significant in the other 3 (rho ranging -0.09 to +0.12, all p>0.15).

pupil_mean vs muae_baseline_power: SIGN FLIPS across sessions with significance in both directions -- sub-V182o_ses-260629 rho=+0.521 p=1.7e-12 (n=160), sub-V198o_ses-230719_rec rho=+0.400 p=2.0e-6 (n=132), but sub-C31o_ses-230823_rec rho=-0.264 p=5.5e-4 (n=168) and sub-V182o_ses-260710 rho=-0.356 p=2.1e-6 (n=168) are significant in the OPPOSITE direction. This sign inconsistency across sessions is itself an important finding: it argues against a single, stable, corpus-wide pupil<->MUAe relationship at this coarse (whole-probe-area) spatial scale, and for session-specific (possibly channel/electrode-configuration-specific) structure instead.
pupil_mean vs pre_event_firing_rate_hz: significant positive in only 1/6 sessions (sub-V182o_ses-260629 rho=0.421 p=3.0e-8 n=160), null elsewhere.

gaze_dist_from_center vs any neural quantity: weaker and less consistent than pupil -- only 2 nominally significant cells out of 18 (sub-C31o_ses-230823_rec vs lfp_baseline_power rho=-0.163 p=0.035; sub-V182o_ses-260629 vs muae_baseline_power rho=0.203 p=0.010, and vs pre_event_firing_rate_hz rho=0.176 p=0.026), both modest effect sizes.

sub-V182o_ses-260629 stands out as the session with the STRONGEST and most numerous behavior-neural correlations across all three neural quantities and both behavioral features -- worth flagging as a session to look at more closely in any follow-up, rather than treating the 6-session average as representative of every session.
task4_covariation_summary.interpretation: The pattern -- real, sometimes strong (|rho| up to 0.52) per-session correlations, but inconsistent in sign and significance across sessions -- is consistent with pupil/gaze carrying SOME plausible pre-event state information beyond the current amplitude-only LFP-baseline gain proxy (which is the goal this audit was asked to check for), but does NOT establish a stable, corpus-wide relationship usable as a drop-in universal covariate without session-specific calibration. This descriptive finding does not by itself resolve whether pupil/gaze would fix the FPR=1.00 failure mode documented for the existing amplitude-only proxy -- that requires the separate synthetic gain-confound benchmark this task was explicitly instructed NOT to attempt here.
